question: to the Commission Wouter Beke (PPE) Subject:

Ongoing geopolitical instability, combined with tight global liquefied natural gas (LNG) and crude oil markets, is limiting the availability of flexible energy supplies. This comes as Member States enter the critical storage filling and winter preparation period. Chapter V of the EU Methane Regulation introduces new monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) requirements for importers of natural gas, LNG and crude oil. Industry stakeholders and Member States have expressed concerns that important implementing measures are not yet available. This creates legal and practical uncertainty for importers required to comply with the new obligations. Such uncertainty could result in cargoes being delayed, reduced or diverted away from the EU. This would weaken security of supply and diversification, while increasing upward pressure on prices. 1.
Does the Commission acknowledge that several measures required for compliance with Chapter V may not be available far enough in advance of 1 January 2027 to allow importers to prepare adequately?

Can the Commission explain the legal and operational basis on which importers will be expected to demonstrate compliance with Chapter V from 1 January 2027 in the absence of the necessary compliance tools?
Is the Commission considering a targeted amendment to postpone the MRV requirements under Chapter V for importers until the necessary compliance infrastructure is in place?
